newsitem.title: UK: UK government unveils new legislative programme.
newsitem.headline: UK government unveils new legislative programme.

text.p: The British government on Wednesday announced its legislative programme for the new parliamentary session, the last before an election due by May at the latest.

The programme, unveiled by Queen Elizabeth in a traditional ceremony, includes 13 bills, ranging from a crackdown on crime to moves to tighten school discipline, most of which were promised at the Conservative conference earlier this month.
The following is a list of the bills, including background details provided by the government.
- Northern Ireland: Decommissioning of Weapons
This would give the government the necessary statutory powers for whatever detailed arrangements are made in Northern Ireland for the scrapping or decommissioning of guerrilla arms.
- Education Bill
This bill, trailed by Education Secretary Gillian Shephard at the Conservative conference, is aimed at tightening school discipline and giving schools more freedom to select pupils.
Schools would be given the power to detain pupils without parental consent and parents would lose the right to choose a school when a child has been excluded from two or more schools.

Different types of school would be allowed to select a proportion of pupils by ability, with grant-maintained schools allowed to select up to 50 percent. Grant-maintained schools would also be allowed to expand to meet local needs.
- Crime (Sentences) Bill
This would introduce automatic life terms for those convicted of a second serious violent or sexual offence and minimum terms for persistent drug dealers and burglars.
- Police Bill
This would establish a national crime squad for England and Wales and establish a criminal records agency.
- Firearms Bill
This would ban all handguns over .22 calibre in the wake of the massacre of 16 children and their teacher at a primary school in the Scottish town of Dunblane in March.
- Merchant Shipping and Maritime Security Bill
This would bring in moves to improve prevention and control of marine pollution and to deal with liability and compensation.
- Channel Tunnel Rail Link Bill (Remaining Stages)
This bill, to allow transfer of the Channel Tunnel Rail Link to the private sector, is not new, but carried over to the new session after completing its Lords select committee stage.
- Primary Health Care Bill
This would allow local doctors and dentists to agree local contractual arrangements on a voluntary basis instead of the current national contract to meet local needs.
- Social Security Fraud Bill
This would allow information on different databases to be compared to detect fraud and ensure effective prosecution of those who conceal information or make false statements.
- Local Government and Rating Bill
This would provide non-domestic rates relief for small general stores and post offices in rural villages.
- Crime and Punishment (Scotland) Bill
This would abolish automatic early release from Scottish prisons and introduce automatic life sentences in Scotland for people convicted for the second time of serious sexual and violent offences.
- Transfer of Crofting Estates (Scotland) Bill
The bill would allow the government to dispose of land on publicly owned crofting estates to trusts representing crofters.
- Civil Procedure Bill
The bill is designed to simplify civil proceedings to reduce the cost of proceedings and encourage alternative settlements.

The government said it would also publish draft bills on the introduction of voluntary identity cards and on measures to help people make better provision for their long term care needs in old age, to encourage further discussion. -- London newsroom 0171 542 7768
